title: Sharp Arm-Mean and ATE Bounds with Imperfect Instruments and Exact Aggregate Support
banked_reason: D0.5.G graded the sound delivered package subfield with paper_score_ceiling 6.6 below the field floor 7.4 and salvageable=false.
gap_reasons: They do not deliver the adaptive contracting procedure or matching general boundary rate posed in oeq:boundary-adaptive-inference, and the statistical lower result is confined to a constructed SDC two-point experiment.

The leading-journal score is constrained by the fixed finite grid, known support endpoints, conservative binary-treatment inference, and absence of an actual reanalysis demonstrating how much the support-filtered set changes the cited applications.
The TL;DR's phrase 'covers the whole exact set' slightly overstates the theorem, which covers the sharp closure of an identified set that need not itself be closed under exact-support restrictions.
proof_attempt_summary: The run proved the finite-grid aggregate-support pruning and sharp-closure package, including all-arm transfer, a robust strict-improvement family, exact rational certificates, and a known-pair root-n boundary minimax result. Correctness and decision referees passed, but the field-tier claim collapsed at the novelty gate because the adaptive contracting procedure and general boundary rate remain open, inference is conservative and specialized, and no cited application was reanalyzed. The sound package is retained at subfield tier for a future re-raise that solves the adaptive OEQ or materially broadens the model or empirical analysis.
tldr: For finite imperfect-instrument cells, SDC and SDC-plus-LEI reduce target-arm identification to bounded completion polytopes, and exact aggregate support retains exactly the positive-slack branches. Unrestricted cone duals give sharp arm closures and conditional product coupling gives the sharp ATE closure; if the all-arm Ban--Kédagni class is nonempty, its exact target-arm and ATE identified sets coincide with those of the target-arm class. The rational center yields \([711/1100,911/1100]\), strictly inside the normalized outer union, and positive LP margins make this strict inclusion persist on an open two-parameter beta neighborhood of \((79/100,17/20)\). A legal three-cell SDC family has minimum positive slack \(3\varepsilon/2\), a fixed Hausdorff jump, and exact known-pair minimax risk \(3/20\) for every \(\varepsilon_n=o(n^{-1/2})\). Binary-treatment Hoeffding projection covers the whole exact set in finite samples.
gap: Ban and Kédagni impose exact aggregate support equality but derive normalized valid bounds and explicitly leave sharpness unresolved. Their formulas do not decide whether an algebraically feasible sign branch admits the required full support.
fill: The paper supplies the positive-slack eligibility equivalence, unrestricted-cone sharp endpoints, simultaneous ATE completion, exact strict and discontinuity examples, a quantitative minimax boundary result, and a conservative finite-sample whole-set confidence region.
